title: Analyzing Endocytosis in Budding Yeast Using Chemically Induced Dimerization of FKBP
author: Lamb, Di Pietro
materials: Difco Yeast Nitrogen Base (YNB) w/o Amino Acids

steps.title: Revive strain and grow starter culture
steps.instruction: Streak the yeast strain from a glycerol stock onto a YPD agar plate, incubate the plate upside down at 30 °C for 2–3 days until single colonies of 1–2 mm appear; store plates upside down, sealed with parafilm at 4 °C for up to 1 month. The next day inoculate one colony into 3 mL synthetic complete (SC) medium in a disposable culture tube (use a 14 mL tube for volumes ≤5 mL, or a 20 mL tube for volumes 5–10 mL).

substeps.instruction: Incubate plate upside down at 30 °C for 2–3 days.
When 1–2 mm colonies appear, store plates upside down with parafilm at 4 °C (up to 1 month).
Inoculate a single colony into 3 mL SC medium in appropriate tube.

steps.title: Incubate starter culture with agitation
steps.instruction: Place the culture tube on a rotator (or shaker) in a dark location at 30 °C for 12–16 h; alternatively incubate at 20–22 °C for slower growth, keeping constant agitation (shaking or rotating).

steps.title: Open time‑lapse image and select mother cell
steps.instruction: Using SlideBook 6 (or any comparable image‑analysis program), open the time‑lapse series and locate an actively budding mother cell; endocytic patches will appear as punctate structures along the plasma membrane.

steps.title: Create masks for fluorescence measurement
steps.instruction: In SlideBook choose Analyze > Create Mask, then generate three regions via Analyze > Mask Generation: (i) the endocytic patch of interest, (ii) the cytosol of the mother cell (excluding nucleus and vacuole), and (iii) background outside the cell.

steps.title: Calculate peak patch‑to‑cytosol ratio
steps.instruction: Track the patch over time, record the average fluorescence intensity of each mask for the frame where the patch intensity is maximal, subtract the background intensity from both patch and cytosol values, then compute the ratio = (patch − background)/(cytosol − background). Ensure the cytosol mask excludes the vacuole and nucleus; adjust image contrast or use a DIC image to identify these organelles.

steps.title: Determine patch lifetime
steps.instruction: Visually identify the first frame where the patch appears, count the number of consecutive frames the patch remains visible, and multiply by the frame interval (e.g., 15 frames × 1 s = 15 s lifetime).

steps.title: Repeat analysis across cells and conditions
steps.instruction: For each time‑lapse image, perform steps 3–6 on the first five endocytic patches in five different mother cells (total 25 patches). Repeat the entire analysis on a second time‑lapse image (additional 25 patches) to obtain data from 50 patches. Carry out the full workflow for both AP20187‑treated and ethanol‑treated samples.

steps.title: Compare treatment effects
steps.instruction: Calculate the average peak patch/cytosol fluorescence ratio and the average patch lifetime for AP20187‑treated cells and for ethanol‑treated cells, then compare the two sets of values to assess the effect of FKBP homodimerization on endocytosis.
